events.title: Birth of George Washington
events.description: George Washington, the first President of the United States, was born in Westmoreland County, Virginia. He later commanded the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War and presided over the Constitutional Convention of 1787.
events.significance: Washington's leadership set enduring precedents for the American presidency, including the peaceful transfer of power, and he is regarded as one of the Founding Fathers of the United States.

events.title: Adams-Onis Treaty Signed
events.description: Spain and the United States signed the Adams-Onis Treaty, under which Spain ceded Florida to the United States and the two nations defined their boundary along the western edge of the Louisiana Purchase.
events.significance: The treaty expanded U.S. territory, settled long-standing border disputes, and advanced American continental expansion in the early 19th century.

events.title: Miracle on Ice
events.description: At the Winter Olympics in Lake Placid, New York, the United States men's ice hockey team, composed of amateur and collegiate players, defeated the heavily favored Soviet Union team 4-3.
events.significance: Played during the Cold War, the victory became a symbol of American national pride and is considered one of the greatest upsets in sports history. The U.S. went on to win the gold medal.

events.title: Execution of White Rose Members
events.description: Sophie Scholl, her brother Hans Scholl, and Christoph Probst, members of the White Rose student resistance group in Nazi Germany, were executed by guillotine after being convicted of treason for distributing anti-Nazi leaflets at the University of Munich.
events.significance: Their courage became a lasting symbol of non-violent resistance to tyranny and moral opposition to the Nazi regime.

events.title: Dolly the Sheep Cloning Announced
events.description: Scientists at the Roslin Institute in Scotland announced that they had successfully cloned an adult mammal, a sheep named Dolly, using somatic cell nuclear transfer.
events.significance: Dolly's creation was a milestone in biotechnology, igniting worldwide scientific and ethical debate about cloning, stem cell research, and genetic engineering.
